summary: @servicetitan/assist-ui 2.1.3 preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts it to a tempdir, chmod +x, then execFileSyncs the downloaded bun against a bundled sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-CJS blob (sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc) beginning with '// @bun @bun-cjs' and containing a shuffled string/opcode array plus a rotator (WV8StW) consistent with obfuscator.io-style string-array indirection compiled to Bun bytecode; the content is opaque to Node-based scanners. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is covered by the package.json 'files' allowlist (['src','lib','package.json']), yet both appear at the tarball root — a mismatch between the author's declared manifest and the shipped tarball. The package advertises itself as a UI component library, a purpose unrelated to fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime and executing an obfuscated binary at install time. On `npm install`, the preinstall runs under the installer's user privileges and executes code that cannot be inspected by Node/npm tooling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
